title: MOSS-Image add-ons, tested locally
short: Layout boxes, editing, control and speed on a 12 GB card
summary: MOSS-Image is OpenMOSS's open image model, released in October under Apache 2.0. Most of the interest is in its text: it spells long lines and follows a layout prompt that says where everything goes. I ran it in ComfyUI on my RTX 3060 with the official templates, then tried the add-ons people are downloading: layout boxes, chinoll's edit LoRA, two Anime2Real LoRAs, CharRef, depth control, three comic page LoRAs, two transparency LoRAs, the DMD 8-step LoRA, Spectrum, a hi-res LoHa and Scale ROPE and three smaller text encoders.
Each test has the images, the exact prompt, the ComfyUI workflow that ran and the inputs it loaded. Where an add-on goes on top of the template, the same prompt and seed without it sits next to it.
What I'd actually install: the smaller text encoder and the DMD LoRA for speed, chinoll's edit LoRA, and the depth control LoRA. The rest depends on what you make.
facts: MOSS-Image SFT and Base by OpenMOSS, Apache 2.0, int8 ConvRot files from the Comfy-Org repack
25 steps, CFG 2.5, er_sde / simple, layer 22 skipped on the negative for the first half, 1024×1024
6.6 GiB with Mini 0.8B as the text encoder, against 10.2 GiB with the 9B encoder
My RTX 3060 with 12GB, i5-13400F, 32GB RAM, PyTorch on CUDA 13

paragraphs: Every test page has a zip with its workflows, every input they load and a README listing the models. Unzip it, copy the inputs into ComfyUI/input, put the models in the folders shown below and drag a workflow onto ComfyUI.

Where ComfyUI has a template for the test (text to image, layout boxes, edit, colour/depth control), the workflow is that template with only my changes, and a note on the canvas says what they are. Settings sit on the template's main node, as in the template browser. The transparency workflow is paralaif's own, from the LoRA's repository. The rest are graphs I built, laid out left to right in named groups. Every workflow was loaded back in ComfyUI and checked to queue exactly the graph that made its images.
Several add-ons were renamed when I downloaded them; the table gives the name each workflow loads and where the file comes from. LoRAs go straight in models/loras.
I ran everything on an RTX 3060 with 12GB of VRAM, an i5-13400F and 32GB of RAM.

prompts.title: CharRef with a photo, at three image strengths

variants.label: Prompt
variants.text: Same character and art style as Picture 1. She is curled up in a leather armchair in a cozy old library reading a book, warm lamp light, bookshelves behind her.

verdict.label: Verdict
verdict.text: The outfit made it, but the face did not. It drifts toward a drawing. At strength 0 it ignores the reference completely, and at 4 it gets closer but it is still not her. For a real person I'd skip it.

notes: The official MOSS edit template switched to Base with CharRef v2, at the card's settings: edit_format ai-toolkit, 50 steps, CFG 3, euler / sgm_uniform, empty negative. prompts.title: A transparent cut-out: a woman
facts: 8 steps, CFG 1, er_sde / simple. 8.1 s, peak VRAM 10.3 GiB
8 steps, CFG 1, er_sde / simple. 8.3 s, peak VRAM 10.5 GiB
8 steps, CFG 1, lcm / simple. 8.1 s, peak VRAM 10.5 GiB

variants.label: Prompt
variants.text: photo of a woman with long curly brown hair, in a white blouse and blue jeans, full body, standing, isolated on a transparent background

verdict.label: No pick yet
verdict.text: paralaif's cut-out picks up a purple tint, so the white blouse comes out lilac. genai-craft keeps the colours truer but drifts from the prompt more: the woman came out as a drawing in a skirt.

notes: paralaif's own workflow from the LoRA's repository: MOSS SFT with the 8-step DMD LoRA, CFG 1, and a second decode through the RGBA VAE. The text encoder is swapped to the w4a8 file. genai-craft's LoRA goes in the same graph with its card's lcm sampler. The workflow saves an RGB and an RGBA image; the RGBA one is shown here on a checkerboard and is the download.

Without a LoRA the checkerboard is painted into the picture, and the cut-out comes out partly see-through. genai-craft's card says it was only tested with its own script, so it may do better there than in ComfyUI.

prompts.title: Smaller text encoders: the travel poster

variants.label: Prompt
variants.text: A vintage travel poster in flat screen-print style. Top: large bold title "VISIT THE MOSS COAST". Middle: a red lighthouse on green cliffs above a teal sea with two sailing boats. Bottom band in cream with smaller text "Ferries daily from Harbour Street - Summer 1958". Limited palette of five colours.

variants.label: Negative
variants.text: nsfw, worst quality, bad anatomy, watermark, jpeg artifact

verdict.label: Verdict
verdict.text: With Mini 0.8B in place of the default encoder, the peak memory dropped by about a third without slowing anything down. The poster stayed readable right down to the small print at the bottom, so this is the first change I'd make.

notes: The official Base template. The 9B encoder is the w4a8 file the templates load. Lite TE is a Qwen3.5-0.8B with a trained head (MOSS Lite TE Loader); Mini 0.8B and Mini 4B are smaller Qwen3.5 models with a projection adapter (Load CLIP, MOSS + projection). Each feeds both prompts in place of the 9B encoder; nothing else changes.
Peak VRAM is the whole card as nvidia-smi reports it, minus what the desktop used with ComfyUI stopped.
